motivation: All5 fixed whole-fragment replacements were blocked by sustained notes crossing fixed boundaries. Test a different intervention that preserves all temporal structure, rather than relaxing or rewriting that failed experiment.
hypothesis: Reusing an earlier group-anchor contour may introduce pitch recurrence without cutting held notes; validity, tonal coherence and listener preference are not guaranteed.
control: Unmodified whole8bar output from the same previously observed global5-seed pool, if separately approved. Both arms share the same generated candidate; no seed substitution.
mapping: Sort original groups by strictly increasing onset. Enumerate C groups j=0..len(C)-1. Replace C[j].anchor by ORIGINAL A[j mod len(A)].anchor+2. Do not use modified anchors recursively. A and C need not have equal counts. C shorter consumes only a prefix; C longer cycles A. No interpolation, matching by score, resampling or phase search.
preserved_fields: every note start and end tick
all within-group pitch offsets relative to anchor
changed_fields: Only C-group anchors and corresponding note absolute pitches. Relative intervals between successive groups, register and transitions entering/leaving C can change.

empty_cases.A_empty: intervention blocked: no source anchors; never call silence a melodic return
empty_cases.C_empty: intervention blocked: no target groups; never count unchanged output as successful intervention

no_op_case: If every mapped C anchor equals its original anchor, record no_effect rather than successful nontrivial recurrence. Keep candidate in all-status denominator.
sustained_boundary_semantics: Do not cut or retime any note crossing2304/4608/6912. Membership follows onset only. A note starting before C and sounding inside it keeps its original pitch; a C note sounding into D keeps its mapped pitch until its original end. Validate overlap with ALL original earlier/later groups, not only adjacent groups. Half-open intervals allow end==nextstart.
fail_closed_checks: Exact full-template reconstruction and unchanged ordered temporal/velocity fields
MIDI pitch0..127 after mapping; reject, do not clip or choose alternate shift
No equal-pitch overlapping note intervals, including sustained notes entering/leaving C
Max3 active voices and max256 notes, inherited temporal shape must remain valid
All note endpoints inside9216 and original tail<=384
Identical complete-output exact8-note interval screen against original17train+observed640/921+Dowland21/1691, generated and canonical ordering; joins included, no internal-repeat exemption
reporting: Every candidate and rejection reason, including collisions, pitch range, copy, empty and no_effect
Number and fraction of changed anchors/notes, original and mapped anchor range
A/C group counts, cycle count and remainder in ordinal mapping
Exact preservation assertions for timing, gates, velocities, note/group count, silence and polyphony
All-seed statuses plus complete-only and common-success denominators; no failed-candidate metric imputation
Source/plan/code hashes and old candidate parity if later implemented
interpretation_limits: The proposal follows inspection of Cycle41 failures; not prospective evidence on unseen outputs.
Ordinal group number is not metrical, melodic-voice or phrase alignment.
Group minimum-pitch anchor is not a verified melody voice; preserving chord offsets does not preserve harmonic function.
+2 chromatic shift and cycling may create collisions, large leaps or inappropriate harmony.
Pitch recurrence is imposed by construction; numeric recurrence gain is not evidence of attraction.
Different A/C group counts change contour sampling. No direct claim comparable to successful whole-fragment copying, of which there were zero.
This is not a learned phrase model, new human preference label, or adopted production behavior.
future_permission: A separate frozen implementation/tests/plan and parent review are required before any fit or generation. No change to Cycle41 frozen artifacts or snapshot.
